info.name: MomCare Platform
info.description:
MomCare backend API: Auth (JWT), Organization (hospital settings, confidence threshold), Monitoring (readings, risk assessments, devices).

Setup:
1. Set `base_url` (default http://localhost:8000).
2. Call Auth -> Login -- it auto-saves `access_token` (collection variable) used by every protected request below.
3. The refresh token is an HttpOnly cookie set by Login; Refresh/Logout read it automatically (Postman keeps cookies per domain).
4. Set `pregnancy_id` to a real pregnancy UUID (from the patients API) before running the Monitoring folder.

Conventions:
- Every endpoint works WITH or WITHOUT a trailing slash.
- All endpoints below require `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` except Login.
- IDs are UUID strings throughout -- never integers.
- `source` on a reading is required on every POST: `"device"` or `"manual"`. It is never inferred -- a band can be assigned to a pregnancy while a nurse still enters a separate manual measurement by hand, so the two are independent facts the caller must declare.
- Roles: platform_admin, hospital_admin, provider, nurse, care_manager, patient. Access is hospital-scoped via `request.user.organization`; a request against another hospital's pregnancy resolves to 404, never 403 (a 403 would confirm the record exists elsewhere).
- Pagination envelope on list endpoints: `{count, page, page_size, total_pages, next, previous, results}`.

request.description:
Email + password -> JWT access token. Returns `{ access }`; the refresh token is set as an HttpOnly cookie, not returned in the body. The test script auto-saves `access_token` for every other request in this collection.

A hospital whose review status is not `approved`, or whose account is suspended, is refused sign-in here even with correct credentials.

Reads the HttpOnly refresh cookie set by Login and issues a new access token. Re-reads the user's current role/hospital fresh each time, so a staff member moved to a different hospital does not keep acting as the old one until the refresh token itself expires.
Blacklists the current refresh token and clears the cookie.
The signed-in user's own identity and role.

The signed-in user's own hospital. Includes both `confidence_threshold` (this hospital's own override, or null if it has never set one) and `effective_confidence_threshold` (the number actually used for scoring -- this hospital's override if set, otherwise the platform default). Also includes `region`, derived from `country` and never independently settable.

hospital_admin only. Sets this hospital's own model-confidence threshold (0.000-1.000) -- an assessment scoring below it is flagged for a doctor's review, regardless of risk level. Persisted to the database on the Organization row (`confidence_threshold`); it is a real column, not computed.

Send `{"confidence_threshold": null}` to clear this hospital's override and revert to following the platform default (`MOMCARE_DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD`, 70%) live -- including any future change to that default.

Records one reading event and scores it immediately in the same request: momcare_model.predict() runs against the pregnancy's latest reading right after this save, so the response already reflects whether risk changed.

Every vital is optional -- at least one must be present, or there is nothing to record. `age` is separate from the 9 vitals used for scoring identity purposes. `hemoglobin` usually will not be present here: it comes from a monthly lab report, not a band.

`source` is required: `"device"` if these numbers came from the wearable's own transmission, `"manual"` if a staff member typed them in by hand -- even if a band happens to be assigned to this pregnancy at the same time, since the two facts are independent.

Response adds `risk_changed` (bool) and `risk_level` (the new `final_risk_level`, or null if the risk level did not transition) on top of the saved reading.

Same endpoint as the device example, with `source: "manual"` -- a nurse with a cuff and a thermometer entering numbers by hand. These particular vitals are deliberately dangerous (Hypertensive Crisis / Tachycardia / Severe Anemia / Diabetes) to demonstrate a High-risk transition and the alert it raises.

query.description: Optional ISO datetime -- only readings recorded at or after this moment.

request.description: The single most recent reading event, or `{"reading": null, "total_count": 0}` when there isn't one yet -- deliberately never a fabricated normal-looking value.

`{ current, history }` -- a record of level *transitions*, not one row per reading. Each assessment carries: `risk_level` (the trained model's raw answer) and `final_risk_level` (what is actually acted on -- these differ only when the Africa+Medium->High rule fires); the 5 clinical categories (bp_category, heart_rate_category, temperature_category, glucose_category, hemoglobin_category); `confidence` (the model's own certainty, 0-1); `flagged_for_review` (true when confidence fell below this hospital's effective_confidence_threshold); the doctor-review fields (`review_status`, `confirmed_risk_level`, `verified_by_name`, `verified_at`); and the exact `reading` this judgement was computed from, nested inline.

Note: the threshold value itself is not included here by design -- fetch it separately from Organization > Get My Organization if you need to show confidence and the threshold side by side.

Re-runs scoring against the latest reading without waiting for a new one -- useful after correcting a reading. Returns the new assessment (201) if the level changed, or `{"detail": "No change in risk level.", "current": ...}` (200) if it did not.

Clinicians only (provider, nurse, care_manager) -- a hospital_admin cannot review a clinical assessment. `confirmed_risk_level` is required and must be one of low/medium/high. `review_status` is derived, not chosen: `confirmed` when it matches `final_risk_level`, `corrected` when it does not. The original `risk_level`/`final_risk_level` are never overwritten by a correction.
Adds one unit to this hospital's stock, unassigned. `acquisition` is one of sold / loaned / subsidised.
Puts a band on a wrist. A pregnancy may wear at most one device at a time; a device may be worn by at most one pregnancy.
Takes the band back. Readings already collected are never touched -- they are observations of things that already happened.
